title: Event Infrastructure Plan™
intro: Build the infrastructure behind any event, a conference, fundraiser, festival, market or performance, through The IV Phases™: purpose, ownership, operations and continuity.

nodes.prompt: Define the purpose: what outcome should this event produce, and what should attendees carry away from it?
Identify the stakeholders: attendees, presenters or artists, your team, the venue, sponsors and the surrounding community. Who is the event for first?
State your non-negotiables: the standards this event will not trade for revenue or attendance.

Assign ownership: name one accountable owner for each of program and content, venue and setup, audio-visual and technical, security and crowd safety, welfare and first aid, registration and admission, vendors and hospitality, and volunteers and staff.
Secure authority: which permits, licenses, insurance and venue agreements are required, and who holds each? (Confirm requirements locally.)
Establish the financial plan: costs, revenue sources and the break-even point.
Design attendee flow: registration or ticketing, admission, capacity, circulation, accessibility, and entry and exit.
Set the operating rhythm: the run-of-show from opening to close, the owner of each segment, and who calls each cue.
Confirm technical readiness: sound, screens and lighting, power and redundancy, and a full test before admission.

Establish the safety and welfare protocol: first aid, hydration and climate, accessibility, emergency response, alcohol or other substances as law and venue require, and how an incident is reported and who acts.
Define command and communication: channels, decision rights, and the contingency when the plan fails.
Capture results: attendance, outcomes against purpose, incidents and lessons learned.
Sustain relationships: how presenters or artists, your team, the venue, sponsors and the community are thanked and retained, and what is owed to them after the event.
Document for continuity: contacts, contracts, run sheets and setup plans, in enough detail for another leader to run the next one.
Build the legacy: what would make this event a lasting series, collective or institution that someone else could carry on?
